questions.question: Who among the following leaders was NOT an accused in the Kakori Train Robbery case?
questions.solution:
Bhagat Singh was not involved in the Kakori Train Robbery (1925).
  • Main accused included Ramprasad Bismil, Ashfaqulla Khan, and Roshan Singh.

questions.question: Which of the following regions was annexed by the British East India Company through the Treaty of Yandabo (1826)?
questions.solution:
The Treaty of Yandabo (1826) ended the First Anglo-Burmese War and resulted in the annexation of Assam by the British.
  • This brought the Ahom kingdom under British influence.

questions.question: Who among the following foreign travellers was appointed in the state service by Muhammad bin Tughlaq?
questions.solution:
The Moroccan traveler Ibn Battuta was appointed as a Qazi (Judge) by Muhammad bin Tughlaq.
  • He wrote the book 'Rihla'.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Bhakti sect named 'Pushtimarg'?
questions.solution:
Vallabhacharya was the founder of the Pushtimarg (Path of Grace) sect.
  • He was a major philosopher of the Bhakti Movement and the Shuddhadvaita school.

questions.question: ho among the following was defeated by Aurangzeb in the Battle of Deorai?
questions.solution:
Aurangzeb defeated his brother Dara Shikoh in the Battle of Deorai (1659).
  • This battle finally secured Aurangzeb's position on the Mughal throne.

questions.question: Which among the following is a Harappan city?
questions.solution:
Dholavira is a major Harappan city located in the Rann of Kutch, Gujarat.
  • It is famous for its sophisticated water management system and 10-signboard inscription.

questions.question: The onus of Jallianwala Bagh massacre that happened in 1919 was on which General of the British Army?
questions.solution:
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre (13 April 1919) was ordered by General Dyer.
  • The protest was against the arrest of Dr. Saifuddin Kitchlew and Dr. Satyapal.

questions.question: Which law was imposed in India during the command of General Dyer?
questions.solution:
Martial Law was imposed in Amritsar after the unrest following the Rowlatt Act.
  • Under Martial Law, public gatherings were banned, which General Dyer used as an excuse for the firing.

questions.question: n which year were 30 Rigveda manuscripts dating from 1800 to 1500 BC included in the UNESCO's Memory of the World Register?
questions.solution:
In 2007, 30 manuscripts of the Rigveda were added to UNESCO’s Memory of the World Register.
  • They are preserved at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, Pune.

questions.question: Who among the following Sikh spiritual leaders is said to have provided aid to Jahangir's rebellious son, Khusrau?
questions.solution:
Guru Arjun Dev (the 5th Sikh Guru) was executed by Jahangir for helping his rebellious son Prince Khusrau.
  • He also compiled the Adi Granth.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT among the writings by Lala Lajpat Rai?
questions.solution:
'India Wins Freedom' was written by Maulana Abul Kalam Azad.
  • Lala Lajpat Rai wrote 'Unhappy India' and 'The Story of My Deportation'.

questions.question: वर्ष 1930 में सी. राजगोपालाचारी ने निम्नलिखित में से किस स्थान पर नमक कानून तोड़ा था?
questions.solution:
C. Rajagopalachari led the Vedaranyam Salt Satyagraha in Tamil Nadu in 1930.
  • It was synchronized with Gandhi's Dandi March.

questions.question: किस संत के सम्मान में अकबर ने फ़तेहपुर सीकरी का निर्माण किया था?
questions.solution:
Akbar built Fatehpur Sikri in honor of the Sufi saint Sheikh Salim Chishti.
  • The Buland Darwaza was built there to commemorate the victory over Gujarat.

questions.question: Who was the first woman to be elected as the President of the Indian National Congress?
questions.solution:
Annie Besant was the first woman President of the INC (1917 Calcutta Session).
  • Sarojini Naidu was the first Indian woman President (1925).

questions.question: In which of the following languages were the ancient Buddhist texts written?
questions.solution:
Most ancient Buddhist texts, including the Tripitakas, were written in Pali.
  • Pali was the common language of the people during that era.

questions.question: rom which of the following cities was the Quit India Movement launched by Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution:
The Quit India Movement was launched from Bombay (Gowalia Tank Maidan) in August 1942.
  • It is also known as the August Kranti.

questions.question: What was the name of King Ashoka’s daughter whom he appointed to carry out the duties of a Buddhist missionary?
questions.solution:
Ashoka sent his daughter Sanghamitra and son Mahinda to Sri Lanka to spread Buddhism.
  • They carried a branch of the Bodhi Tree with them.

questions.question: In order to curb the East India Company traders’ unrestrained commercial activities and to bring about some order in territories under the Company control, the British Parliament enacted a series of laws among which the ______ stood first.
questions.solution:
The Regulating Act of 1773 was the first parliamentary act to intervene in the Company's administration in India.
  • It established the office of Governor-General of Bengal.

questions.question: Who among the following is regarded as the founder of Aurangabad city?
questions.solution:
Malik Ambar, the Prime Minister of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate, is credited with founding Aurangabad (originally called Kharki).
  • He was a pioneer in guerrilla warfare in the Deccan.

questions.question: With whom is the 'Patharughat Uprising' associated?
questions.solution:
The Patharughat Uprising (1894) in Assam was a Peasants' uprising against increased land revenue.
  • It is often called the 'Jallianwala Bagh of Assam'.

questions.question: Who among the following was the founder of the Suryavamsi Gajapati dynasty that ruled parts of Orissa and Andhra Pradesh in the 15th century?
questions.solution:
Kapilendra Deva founded the Suryavamsi Gajapati Dynasty in 1434.
  • The dynasty ruled over present-day Odisha and parts of Andhra Pradesh.

questions.question: ho spearheaded the Revolt of 1857 rebellion in Bihar?
questions.solution:
Kunwar Singh (of Jagdishpur/Arrah) spearheaded the 1857 Revolt in Bihar.
  • He was a 80-year-old Zamindar who fought brilliantly against the British.

questions.question: he Caves of Elephanta are predominantly dedicated to which of the following deities?
questions.solution:
The Elephanta Caves (Gharapuri) are primarily dedicated to Lord Shiva.
  • The most famous sculpture here is the Trimurti.

questions.question: ho among the following first deciphered the Brahmi script in 1837?
questions.solution:
James Prinsep, an official of the Calcutta Mint, deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1837.
  • This allowed for the reading of Ashoka’s edicts.

questions.question: ho among the following became the acting Prime Minister of India after the death of Jawaharlal Nehru?
questions.solution:
Gulzarilal Nanda served as acting Prime Minister twice (after Nehru in 1964 and after Shastri in 1966).
  • He was a veteran labor leader and politician.
